decisions.reason: The payoff supplier requires L1, not L2. For X with P(X=n)=n^(-3)/sum_{m>=1}m^(-3), E[X]<infinity but E[X^2]=infinity; taking H(eta,omega)=X makes both payoffs identical and their covariance undefined in the finite-moment interface. The estimator itself remains a well-defined integrable difference. Qualified only the covariance sentence by square-integrability; no payoff-domain restriction was added.

The fixed-support theorem is sound, but its final universal necessity claim is false. Take q(u)=(15/16)(1-u^2)^2 for |u|<1 and zero elsewhere, p_theta(x)=q(x-theta), and H=1. Then integral q=1, q is C1, J=1, S=4u/(1-u^2) on the moving positive support, E[S]=-integral qprime=0, and E[S^2]=15 integral_{-1}^1 u^2 du=10. Thus the score formula holds with finite variance and no boundary contribution despite moving support. Replaced only the false necessity claim by sufficiency; all positive hypotheses/conclusions are retained. Proof 2.1 now explicitly uses the weighted supremum, with a measurable version set to zero on the common exceptional null set, to justify domination by 2G.

The algorithm explicitly labels its tuple (Delta_1,...,Delta_d), and the theorem consistently uses those labels. With the standard relabelling x_i=x(i-1), sum_{i=1}^d a_i Delta_i equals the supplier inner product sum_{k<d} a(k)Delta(k); d=1 has exactly one coordinate and no off-diagonal term. No theorem depends on a coordinate label. Independently checked the C3 central-difference remainder M3 c^2||Delta||^3/6, q_i remainder integrability, independent first/reciprocal moments, symmetry cancellation, and the unbounded measurable reciprocal pull-out after weighted residual integrability. This is valid standard tuple notation, not a mathematical defect.

The local conditional-expectation interface is explicitly restricted to L1 inputs: def-conditional-expectation-given-a-sigma-algebra requires integrable X, and def-conditional-expectation-as-an-ae-class defines its L1 version class. Thus the displayed premise E[W|F]<=B already assumes W=(|Y+|^2+|Y-|^2)sum_i|Delta_i|^(-2) is integrable; it does not invoke an extended nonnegative conditional expectation. F4 is consequently applicable and gives E W=E E[W|F]<=B. The pointwise norm inequality implies G is L2; conditional monotonicity and the scalar second-moment identities summed over coordinates give both bounds. There is no circularity under the actual imported interface.

The Example introduces the radius c without declaring its admissible domain, although both estimators divide by 2c and the imported Definition and variance identity require a positive radius. At c=0 the displayed claims are undefined. Added c>0 to Example and Given. Verified E Z=0 by symmetry and integrability from E Z^2=1, J(theta)=theta, cancellation of the shared Z giving estimate 1, and independent centered unit-variance noises giving (1+1)/(4c^2)=1/(2c^2). AC already supplies the required Countable Choice. No theorem Statement or Definition is changed by this example repair.
